title: We Are South Maui CPAC Meeting of October 16, 2023

issues.title: Maui Research and Technology Park land designation

recap.headline: South Maui plan committee revisits land use maps for Kīhei, Wailea and Mākena
recap.in_60_seconds: The South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee met to make final changes to the plan's land use maps, sub-area by sub-area. No one gave public testimony; two people spoke as resource persons for landowners or businesses, and County planning staff answered questions. A 5–4 vote to return the Pi’ilani Promenade lands to residential fell short of the needed majority, so they stay small town center. A motion to turn Kīhei Mauka into open space and agriculture failed 4–5. The committee voted to make a 23-acre Wailea parcel park, to make four Mākena parcels outside the growth boundary agriculture, and to change three Mākena hotel-resort areas to residential. A proposal to expand a recycling area above the Kīhei wastewater plant, and whether the committee gets more time, were left for later; the next meeting is Wednesday.

parts.title: Opening, roll call and vision statement
presented: Roll call: 2 members absent, 2 arriving late.
Tonight's agenda: review all adopted maps and land use designations, sub-area descriptions (sections 3.1 to 3.5), new policies, historic and scenic sites, and ranking of actions.
Changing an earlier decision needs a motion to amend something previously adopted.
The vice chair read the South Maui vision statement; no testimony was offered before the first item.

next.what: Another member to read the vision statement

parts.title: Sub-area 2: motion to return Pi’ilani Promenade lands to residential
presented: A member moved to return the three Pi’ilani Promenade lots, once called the Megamall lands, to residential, as approved on May 17, 2023.
Supporters said the Land Use Commission shows no change in ownership, the owner missed its 2022 annual report, and the County filed it on September 27, 2023.

Supporters said small town center is commercial by definition and lets an owner build little or no housing; they cited letters from the Kīhei Community Association and Maui Tomorrow backing residential.
Opponents said a 1995 approval and a settlement already allow a 123-lot light industrial plan, the owner wants small town center, and residential could bring less housing because of cultural buffers.

answered.said: The number of homes depends on single-family or multifamily; a 2017 Kīhei Community Association proposal mixed both.
The owner already has some approvals for light industrial, so it could build that before the plan is approved.

next.what: Map decisions go on to the Planning Commission and County Council

parts.title: Sub-area 2: Kīhei Mauka roundabouts and Pi’ilani Promenade buffers
presented: Members voted to remove the park color from roundabouts on the Haleakalā Ranch Kīhei Mauka map.
A member moved to add, on the Pi’ilani Promenade, a road parallel to Pi’ilani Highway for walking and biking, a planted buffer along the highway, and a 100-foot buffer around the cultural reserve.
He said these were 1995 conditions meant to ease traffic and soften the view from the highway.

answered.said: The roundabouts were green because they matched the park designation on the map provided; other Maui roundabouts have no designation but can still be planted.

parts.title: Sub-area 2: motion to make Kīhei Mauka open space and agriculture
presented: The vice chair moved to change Kīhei Mauka from residential and neighborhood center to open space and agriculture, citing written testimony of about 6,500 possible units.
He said the 20-year growth projection is 3,000 to 6,000 homes and roads, schools, water and sewer cannot keep up.
Opponents said Kīhei Mauka is near the high school and jobs, and the project is to be about 80% workforce or affordable housing with a road toward Veterans Highway.
A member said the master-planned project would build its own road sections, leaving the State to build the link to Veterans Highway.

parts.title: Sub-area 2: Maui Research and Technology Park designations
presented: The research park and Kīhei Mauka owners asked to remove open space designations for drainage gulches.
Staff kept gulches as open space to match earlier policies and the West Maui Community Plan.
A motion to make the whole research park special purpose district got no second.
A 0.2-acre employment center strip was called a map error; the committee took a 10-minute break.

parts.title: Sub-area 3: recycling area above the Kīhei wastewater plant
presented: A member moved to expand the growth boundary above the Kīhei wastewater reclamation facility for recycling.
Members said the site runs on 5-year special use permits, which block financing for new equipment.
Earlier notes put the area at 106 acres; the materials recycling facility uses 10 acres and needs 10 more.

raised.concern: A representative of the recycling and compost site said the area needs room to expand and promised to work out narrow allowed uses rather than broad light industrial.

answered.said: Any work would need an archaeological inventory survey and cultural review through the State Historic Preservation Division.
The committee can only recommend, not decide, a growth boundary change.

next.what: Recycling site representative to work with the Kīhei Community Association on allowed uses

parts.title: Sub-area 4: Wailea park parcel, transit corridor and Wailea 670 map
presented: The vice chair moved to change a 23-acre parcel next to the 13-acre Kīlohana county park from residential to park, citing about 3,600 people in Maui Meadows and Wailea in 2020.
The transit corridor square was changed to small town center without objection.
A member asked whether the map title Wailea fits, since the Wailea 670 project reaches toward Mākena.
A member moved to use the developer's map for Wailea 670, then withdrew it after a member who knows the gulches pointed out missing gulches.

raised.concern: A representative of Honuaʻula Partners said its ground-surveyed map is more accurate than the County's LIDAR-based map and asked that the Planning Commission approval be the default.

answered.said: The community plan does not affect the Wailea Community Association, so the map name need not change.

parts.title: Sub-area 5: Mākena
presented: A family property was changed from residential to agriculture without objection.
Four parcels outside the urban growth boundary, one owned by the State, were changed to agriculture; staff could not say who had designated them residential.
A motion to make the Palauea preserve open space was withdrawn after a member read County code allowing a caretaker cottage and other uses.
Three hotel-resort areas, including the Maluaka beach lots and Mākena Resort, were changed to residential; one member recused as an owner.

answered.said: The Palauea preserve is special purpose district because its allowed uses, such as a caretaker cottage, do not fit open space.
All three Mākena resort areas are zoned hotel, which allows short-term rentals.
An extension of the committee's work is on Wednesday's agenda and can only be discussed then.

next.what: Discussion of extending the committee's work, fourth agenda item

parts.title: Closing
presented: The first agenda item was finished with no changes for sub-area 6.
The meeting was adjourned at 8:45 p.m. so the extension could be discussed next time.

next.what: Continue review of remaining agenda items

bills.name: South Maui Community Plan
bills.what: The draft plan whose land use maps and designations the committee is reviewing.

bills.name: Maui Island Plan
bills.what: Island-wide plan that sets the urban and rural growth boundaries the committee can recommend changing.

bills.name: Kīhei-Mākena Community Plan (1998)
bills.what: The current community plan, which members said called for infrastructure alongside development.

bills.name: West Maui Community Plan
bills.what: Recent community plan whose policy keeps gulches as open space, cited as a model.

bills.name: Maui County Code 19.91.030 (Ordinance 2898)
bills.what: Sets allowed uses in the Palauea cultural preserve park district, including caretaker facilities.

votes.what: Return the Pi’ilani Promenade lands to residential
votes.result: Failed, 5 yes to 4 no; members said it lacked the needed majority and the land stays small town center

votes.what: Remove park designation from roundabouts on the Kīhei Mauka map
Add parallel walking and biking road, highway buffer and 100-foot cultural reserve buffer at Pi’ilani Promenade
votes.result: Vote taken; result not announced on the recording

votes.what: Change Kīhei Mauka to open space and agriculture
Expand growth boundary above the Kīhei wastewater plant for recycling
votes.result: Vote taken; result cut off on the recording

votes.what: Change 23-acre parcel next to Kīlohana park from residential to park
Change the transit corridor to small town center
Change a Mākena family property from residential to agriculture
Make four Mākena parcels outside the urban growth boundary agriculture
Change three Mākena hotel-resort areas to residential
votes.result: Passed with 7 votes; one member recused, two abstained

open_questions.question: How many acres, and exactly where, would the Kīhei recycling area expansion cover?
Who designated the four Mākena parcels outside the growth boundary as residential, and why?
Will the committee get more time to finish its review?
Where would money come from for a mauka road parallel to Pi’ilani Highway?

not_on_tracker.topic: Expanding the Kīhei compost and materials recycling site
not_on_tracker.why: The operators say 5-year permits keep them from financing equipment to recycle more of South Maui's waste.

moments.who: A South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
moments.quote: And if we keep the land use designation that we have now, we're saying to them, you can do some residential, you can do all residential, or you might do none.
moments.about: Explains why a CPAC member moved to return the Pi’ilani Promenade lands from small town center to residential in the draft South Maui Community Plan.

moments.quote: They do already have some of their approvals for light industrial.
moments.about: Staff clarify that the Pi’ilani Promenade owner could still build under existing light industrial approvals before the community plan is adopted.

moments.who: A South Maui Community Plan Advisory Committee member
moments.quote: And it has. And we really need to scale back because our infrastructure is barely adequate to maintain what we currently have.
moments.about: A CPAC member argues the draft plan allows far more housing than projected growth and infrastructure can support, in a motion to hold Kīhei Mauka as open space and agriculture.

moments.quote: And then MRTP is saying the entire area should be special purpose district and not include the park designation or the open space designation.
moments.about: Staff explain that the Maui Research and Technology Park has asked for its whole area to be designated special purpose district without park or open space designations in the South Maui Community Plan.
